citations.claim_text:
DOCMATE AI / JUDGES DEMO LIBRARY
Diabetes diagnostic
reference
Adult laboratory thresholds, confirmation, and limits of classification
Laboratory thresholds in nonpregnant adults
LABORATORY HbA1c (A1C) FASTING PLASMA GLUCOSE (FPG)
6.5% or higher 126 mg/dL or higher
Each threshold falls in the diabetes range. Laboratory fasting plasma glucose is measured after a fast
of at least 8 hours. [1, 2]
Confirm with a second result
A second test is generally used to confirm diabetes. Repeated fasting plasma glucose in the diabetes
range on separate draws supports confirmation. [1, 2]
Use symptoms as clinical context
Frequent urination (polyuria), increased thirst (polydipsia), and fatigue can occur with diabetes. These
symptoms occur across diabetes types. Check the documented laboratory results before confirming
the diagnosis in an evidence review. [1, 3]
Keep the diagnosis and its subtype separate
These glucose tests can establish diabetes mellitus. Classifying the subtype requires additional clinical
assessment. If A1C and glucose disagree, review test reliability and possible factors affecting A1C. [1,
2]
Sources
[1] NIDDK. Diabetes Tests & Diagnosis
[2] NIDDK. Diabetes & Prediabetes Tests
[3] CDC. Symptoms of Diabetes

citations.claim_text:
DOCMATE AI / SYNTHETIC TEST DATA 04
SYNTHETIC RECORDS / FX-107 TO FX-109
Blood pressure and metabolic
documentation
Preserve units, dates and the difference between a reading and a diagnosis. FX-107 | Orchid-42 | Two blood pressure readings
Record. Adult, 61. A clinic intake lists an upper-arm measurement of 148/94 mmHg and a later entry on a
separate day of 142/90 mmHg. Both are recorded observations. Evidence statement. Orchid-42 lists 148/94 mmHg on the first visit and 142/90 mmHg on the second
visit. Record limitation. Measurement conditions and clinician assessment are unrecorded. FX-108 | Iris-08 | Blood pressure measurement disagreement
Record. Adult, 46. The home diary shows 131/82 mmHg at 07:30. The clinic intake shows 151/92 mmHg
at 14:20. Device validation is unknown. Evidence statement. Iris-08 labels 131/82 mmHg as home and 151/92 mmHg as clinic. Record limitation. Measurement technique, repeat readings and device validation are missing. FX-109 | Lotus-27 | Glucose with unknown fasting status
Record. Adult, 52. Glucose 168 mg/dL was transcribed from a point-of-care screen. The meal timing field
is empty. No interpretation was entered. Evidence statement. Lotus-27 records glucose of 168 mg/dL with fasting status unknown. Record limitation. Confirm specimen, timing, device and clinician interpretation.

citations.claim_text:
DOCMATE AI / SYNTHETIC TEST DATA 05
SYNTHETIC RECORDS / FX-110 TO FX-112
Infection concern and uncertainty
Separate an observation, a suspected source and a confirmed finding. FX-110 | Ember-38 | Infection concern with mental status change
Record. Adult, 70. A caregiver described new confusion at 16:20 after a reported infection. The triage
note records an urgent clinician-review flag as a fictional workflow event. Evidence statement. Ember-38 records caregiver-reported new confusion at 16:20. Record limitation. Baseline mental status, examination and measurement context are unavailable. FX-111 | Cinder-22 | Urine test status and attribution
Record. Adult, 58. On the first day a urine specimen was requested. The second-day note says the
specimen was received. There is no result, organism or diagnosis in this fixture. Evidence statement. Cinder-22 says the specimen was received and the urine result remains pending. Record limitation. Result, specimen quality and clinician assessment are absent. FX-112 | Flint-65 | Explicit denial and later uncertainty
Record. Adult, 36. The intake explicitly records no chills. The follow-up contains no entry for chills. The
entry “not reassessed” applies to the follow-up only. Evidence statement. Flint-65 records no chills at intake and no reassessment of chills at follow-up. Record limitation. Do not carry the intake denial forward as a new observation.
